dedupe_keys.name: nlr resource planning model rpm regional power system capacity expansion and hourly dispatch with nodal focus region

description: The Resource Planning Model (RPM) is a National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) capacity expansion model for a regional power system such as a utility service territory, state or balancing authority, drawing on NLR's national ReEDS model and production cost simulation. Contents: an optimisation that finds the least-cost investment and dispatch over a 20-year horizon for conventional and renewable generation, storage and transmission; the grid is represented down to individual units and lines in a focus region with a zonal representation of the rest of the interconnection, and dispatch runs on sampled hourly time steps with energy balance, reserves and generator constraints. Transmission is modelled as a transport (pipe-flow) or linearised DC power flow; the model treats wind and solar location, variability and uncertainty, capacity credits, curtailment, congestion and cycling costs. Producer: NLR Energy Systems Analysis. Coverage: versions for regions of the Western Interconnection are available for research use and an Eastern Interconnection version is under development; published work includes 11 Western Interconnection scenarios to 2030. Format and access: documentation and reports on the NLR page; the model is available for research applications. Licence: not stated on the NLR page. Caveats: access terms are not spelled out; the Eastern version was not yet released. Simulation uses: regional generation and transmission expansion planning and renewable integration studies. Related records: model-reeds, platform-sienna and model-pras.
